examples.question_text:
The numbers of books borrowed by 10 students are $0,1,2,1,3,2,1,5,2,0$.
(a) Construct a frequency table and a dot plot.
(b) How many students borrowed exactly 1 book?
(c) How many borrowed more than 2 books?
(d) What percentage borrowed at least 3 books?
Construct an ordered stem-and-leaf plot for $42,18,24,54,22,18,47,21,56$. Use all digits except the last as the stem and give a key.
examples.solution_text:
Use stems 1 to 5. Write each final digit beside its stem, then order the leaves from smallest to largest. Keep stem 3 with no leaves because there are no values in the 30s.

$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\\hline1&8\;8\\2&1\;2\;4\\3&\\4&2\;7\\5&4\;6\end{array}$

Key: $2\mid4$ means 24. Each leaf represents one data value.

examples.question_text:
The stem-and-leaf plot shows scores.

$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\\hline2&3\;8\\3&1\;5\;5\\4&0\;6\\5&1\end{array}$

Key: $2\mid3$ means 23.
What is the highest score?
examples.solution_text: Read the largest stem and its largest leaf. The final row has stem 5 and leaf 1, so the highest score is 51.

(a) The salad column reaches halfway between 6 and 8, so 7 salad sandwiches were sold.

(b) Read both column heights: chicken is 9 and cheese is 4. Subtract to compare them.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}9-4\\&=5\text{ sandwiches}\end{aligned}$

(a) Read the height of the column centred on score 4. Its frequency is 5.

(b) The tallest columns are centred on scores 3 and 5. Both have frequency 7, so both scores are most frequent.

coverage.summary: Authored five worked examples covering every distinct accepted assessment method, using adapted booklet tasks and different values. Questions and solutions remain separate and editable; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Arithmetic continuation rows include phantom equals gutters. Diagrams use black marks, unshaded columns, 10 pt ordinary labels and 8.5 pt ticks. Practice and quiz content were classified only and remain unchanged. Independent review and final rendered visual verification remain pending.

examples.derivation: Counting the supplied observations gives frequencies 2,3,3,1,0,1 for values 0–5, matching the table and dot stacks. Exactly 1 book: 3 students. More than 2 books: 1+0+1=2 students. Total: 10 students; at least 3 books: 2/10×100%=20%. Construction, counting and percentage methods follow the supplied frequency-table and dot-plot teaching and exercises.

Sorting independently gives 18,18,21,22,24,42,47,54,56. The leaves are 1|8 8; 2|1 2 4; 3 empty; 4|2 7; 5|4 6. All nine observations are retained, repeated leaves are preserved, and the key correctly reads 2|4 as 24. Empty intermediate stems follow the supplied teaching.
The plot represents 23,28,31,35,35,40,46,51. The largest occupied stem is 5 and its leaf is 1, giving the highest score 51. This directly adapts the supplied highest-score exercise.

The equal-width separated columns encode cheese 4, salad 7 and chicken 9. The vertical scale places salad halfway between 6 and 8. Chicken exceeds cheese by 9−4=5 sandwiches. Reading and subtracting column heights match the supplied column-graph exercise.

The touching columns centred on scores 2,3,4,5 have frequencies 3,7,5,7 respectively. Score 4 therefore has frequency 5. The maximum frequency is 7, shared by scores 3 and 5. Both interpretations follow the supplied histogram exercises.

review.summary: All 16 exact assessment locators are mapped, and the five examples cover every distinct assessed method with source-supported adaptations and different values. No existing examples require preservation checks. Questions and solutions are separate; continuation gutters are correct, and solution prose/math can inherit the confirmed renderer blue. Diagram data, labels and annotations are consistent. No syllabus exception or solid-geometry review is needed. Accepted practice/quiz mathematics was not re-audited. Final rendered typography and layout verification remains a later stage.
